text:
maria-support: Customer reported intermittent truncation of tool-call args during SSE streaming. They say the JSON payload for the tool call is cut mid-object on resume/keepalive, causing schema validation failures on our side. stack: Node SDK v0.9.2, nginx ingress, Cloudflare in front. Repro attached below. Anyone seen keepalive chunk splitting cause this?

maria-support: minimal repro they sent: curl -> keepalive SSE with chunked transfer, toolcall payload gets a tail cut off. Logs show terminal chunk missing closing brace.

maria-support: curl example they used:
```bash
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate \
  -d $'event: open\\n
: keepalive
' \
  --data-binary $'{"model":"gpt-psi","input":"call_tool","tool_call": {"name":"charge_customer","args": {"invoice_id":"inv_123","amount": 99}'
```

maria-support: on our side we receive chunks: 
- chunk1: `{"model":"gpt-psi","input":"call_tool","tool_call":{"name":"charge_customer","args":{"invoice_id":"inv_123","amount": 99}`
- chunk2 (keepalive): `
: keepalive
`
- chunk3: never arrives (or arrives but as separate TCP segment after connection resume) so JSON stays open. Client reports we then respond with schema error.

tom-eng: ugh. this smells like chunk boundary + proxy inserting keepalive lines. if the SSE heartbeat is injected as its own chunk between two halves of a JSON token, the consumer concatenates verbatim and ends up with `99
: keepalive` inside the JSON stream. our parser expects pure JSON frames and chokes.

tom-eng: quick check — are they using `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and no content-length? proxies/ingress will often split at N bytes and also inject keepalives.

elaine-ops: i pulled the request-id from their support ticket (req-id: rq_0b9f2). looking at ingress logs, upstream sent 3 chunks within ~120ms. cloudflare returned keepalive 2nd. ingress nginx log shows chunk sizes 8192 / 1 / 4096 bytes. that tiny middle chunk is the keepalive line.

jordan-ml: from the runtime side, our SSE handler expects each event to be a complete JSON object in a single event payload. we do have code that tries to reassemble across chunks, but it strips any lines that start with `:` (SSE comment) which in this case gets injected into the middle of a JSON string and becomes invalid.

maria-support: customer claims this only happens when they enable "edge keepalive" on their CDN. disabled keepalive -> no repro. enabled -> ~1 in 100 requests fail with truncated args.

tom-eng: can we be more tolerant in the parser? Options: 1) reassemble raw byte stream ignoring SSE comment boundaries and then extract the JSON object by balancing braces OR 2) require callers to send final newline + explicit `event: toolcall_complete` frame so we only parse after complete marker.

jordan-ml: option 1 is doable but risky — we'd need to ignore SSE comment lines (starting with `:`) that may appear inside JSON if split. safer: treat SSE comments as separators and never allow them inside JSON; instead buffer until we see a fully balanced JSON object. implement brace counting across event boundaries and drop any bare-colon lines outside quoted strings.

elaine-ops: quick workaround for affected customers: force the SDK to send smaller payloads (so keepalive won't split) or set the CDN to not insert keepalive comments. i can also add a temporary ingress rule to coalesce small chunks for their tenant.

maria-support: customer wants a fix on our side — they can't change CDN for compliance. can we ship a quick tolerance patch to reassembly logic and a small test? they provided a failing curl script.

tom-eng: i'll prototype a conservative reassembly: track open braces, track string escapement state, ignore full SSE comment lines (lines that start with `:` and end with `\n`) only when outside of a string, and continue accumulating until brace count returns to zero. if timeout without closure -> emit schema error as before. this should handle keepalive injects between tokens.

tom-eng: patch plan:
- add incremental byte-buffer in sse_stream_parser (non-blocking)
- on receipt of any new chunk, feed into the buffer, but strip lines matching `^:\s*.*$` only when not inside a JSON string; otherwise keep them as bytes (shouldn't happen if above logic correct).
- attempt to detect complete JSON object by brace counting outside strings and return object when balanced.

repro-bot: Suggested unit tests: 1) chunked-json-with-comment-in-middle (split a JSON token and insert `: keepalive` chunk), 2) chunked-json-within-string-boundary (ensure strings with `:` preserved), 3) long-array-split-across-chunks.

jordan-ml: major caveat: brace counting must handle nested arrays/objects and escaped quotes. use a tiny state machine. i can add test vectors.

elaine-ops: i've queued an ingress tweak for their tenant to mitigate immediately (coalesce-chunks=true). will keep disabled as long-term is a runtime fix.

maria-support: customer is appreciative of the mitigation but asks for an ETA on the runtime fix. can we do a patch release this week?

tom-eng: i can do a small patch + unit tests, run in staging tomorrow. if all green, aim for canary on Thursday and rollout Friday. i'll post PR link when ready.

maria-support: thanks — please include an entry in the support ticket with workaround steps and ask them to retry after canary. attaching logs to the ticket now. :pray:

jordan-ml: one more note — also look at websocket fallback. websockets tend to avoid injected `:` keepalive lines. for customers who can switch transports that is another mitigation.

maria-support: noted, will offer ws fallback in the ticket as temporary option.

elaine-ops: FYI added monitoring alert: if we see `schema_error` correlated with `sse_keepalive_injection` pattern > 0.1% over 5m for any tenant, trigger paging.

maria-support: perfect. i'll close the slack thread when PR + canary links posted. thanks all.
